note: Known-answer vectors for location messages (WIRE_SPEC section 14). Generated by tools/katgen/location with the Go standard library only. User ids and message ids are test UUIDs derived from public labels; the share keys are test values. Doubles are carried as the hexadecimal IEEE 754 bits (deg_bits, m_bits, lat_bits, lon_bits, acc_bits): a decimal text may parse to a neighbouring double in some library. Clients pin the SHA-256 of this file.

constants.USER_ID_FORMAT: 36-character lowercase canonical UUID text, exactly as the server sends it

positive.why: ids are the bytes of the string the server sent, preceded by one length byte, whatever their length (the server issues 36-character ids; this pins the length byte)

positive.name: multibyte_ids
positive.why: the length byte counts the UTF-8 bytes of the id (the server issues lowercase UUID text; this pins the byte rule)

positive.name: long_ids
positive.why: 255-byte ids, the largest the length byte allows

negative.name: flip_version_to_0
negative.why: the first byte is the version

negative.name: flip_version_to_2
negative.why: the first byte is the version

negative.name: flip_counter_bit
negative.why: the counter is bound by the nonce and the aad

negative.name: flip_counter_high_byte
negative.why: the counter is bound by the nonce and the aad

negative.name: flip_ciphertext_first_bit
negative.why: any bit of the ciphertext

negative.name: flip_ciphertext_last_bit
negative.why: any bit of the ciphertext

negative.name: flip_tag_first_bit
negative.why: any bit of the tag

negative.name: flip_tag_last_bit
negative.why: any bit of the tag

negative.name: wrong_sender_id
negative.why: a server that stamps another sender, or a frame replayed into another conversation, fails authentication

negative.name: wrong_recipient_id
negative.why: the receiver's own id is in the aad

negative.name: swapped_ids
negative.why: sender and recipient are not interchangeable

negative.name: sender_id_prefix
negative.why: an id that is a prefix of the real one is another id (the length byte is in the aad)

negative.name: uppercase_sender_id
negative.why: the aad carries the bytes of the id string the server sent (lowercase): an id re-serialised through a platform UUID type (upper case) is another id

negative.name: uppercase_recipient_id
negative.why: the receiver's own id is the lowercase string the server issued, never re-serialised through a platform UUID type

negative.name: frame_of_another_share
negative.why: a frame of share B under share A's key

negative.name: same_key_other_sid
negative.why: the sid is the HKDF salt and is in the aad: the same k under another sid is another share

negative.name: truncated_36

negative.name: extended_38

negative.name: empty

negative.name: header_only

negative.name: sealed_with_version_2

negative.name: flags_bit2
negative.why: bits 2 to 7 of the flags MUST be 0

negative.name: flags_bit7
negative.why: bits 2 to 7 of the flags MUST be 0

negative.name: iv_9
negative.why: iv is 10..600 in a position frame

negative.name: iv_601
negative.why: iv is 10..600 in a position frame

negative.name: iv_0_in_position_frame

builder_cases.name: canonical
builder_cases.why: the stop of a live share: target is the client message id of the live start

builder_cases.name: target_escaped
builder_cases.why: the target is a JSON string written the canonical way

receiver_cases.name: member_order_free
receiver_cases.why: members may appear in any order

receiver_cases.name: whitespace_around
receiver_cases.why: JSON whitespace around and between tokens

receiver_cases.name: drop_target_null
receiver_cases.why: null is a value of the wrong type

receiver_cases.name: drop_other_variant
receiver_cases.why: another variant of the control envelope is not a stop

receiver_sequences.name: basic_live_with_staleness
receiver_sequences.why: start, frames, silence until STALE (strictly more than 120 s), a frame that revives it, the final frame, then frames and a stop that change nothing

event.note: the start arrives 2 s after the sender started: endAt = min(R + du, st + du + 600) = R + du
ctr 1: the position moves, fix time = now - age
120 s after the last frame: still ACTIVE (the test is strictly greater)
121 s after the last frame: STALE, the last position is kept
ctr 3: the next valid frame makes it ACTIVE again
the final frame: ENDED (stopped), key and positions deleted
a frame for an ended share is dropped and never brings it back
a stop for an ended share changes nothing; the first reason stays

receiver_sequences.name: order_duplicates_and_late_frames
receiver_sequences.why: the frame with the highest counter wins; a late, reordered or duplicate frame is dropped and never overwrites a newer position

event.note: ctr 3 arrives before ctr 2 (a lost frame is simply superseded)
ctr 2 arrives late: dropped, the position stays ctr 3's
ctr 3 again (a duplicate, here with another position): dropped
ctr 0 can never be newer than the initial state
nothing is newer than the largest counter

receiver_sequences.name: late_start_already_over
receiver_sequences.why: a start delivered after its end time creates an ended card with no key and no position; frames for it are dropped

event.note: st + du + 600 = T0 + 4200 <= R: ENDED (expired) on arrival, k never stored
no key was kept: nothing matches

receiver_sequences.name: late_start_23_hours
receiver_sequences.why: a start delivered 23 hours late of a 24-hour share still has 4200 s left: the end time is st + du + 600

event.note: ENDED (expired) at endAt, no stop and no final frame needed

receiver_sequences.name: end_at_never_grows
receiver_sequences.why: frames never extend a share: it ends at its endAt whatever arrives; to share longer the sender starts a new share, which supersedes the old one

event.note: one second before the end: accepted, endAt is still T0 + 600
at endAt: ENDED (expired), the frame is dropped
a new share is a new row with its own key
the old share's frames still match nothing

receiver_sequences.name: newer_start_supersedes_older
receiver_sequences.why: a start from the same peer ends the previous share; an older start that arrives after a newer one is created ended

event.note: share B starts: A becomes ENDED (superseded), key and position deleted
share C has an older st than B and arrives after it: created ENDED (superseded)

receiver_sequences.name: starts_arrive_in_reverse_order
receiver_sequences.why: the newer share's start arrives first: the older one is born superseded and never ACTIVE

event.note: share B, started later, arrives first
share A, started earlier, arrives later: ENDED (superseded)

receiver_sequences.name: expired_start_does_not_touch_others
receiver_sequences.why: a start that is already over on arrival is recorded ended and leaves a running share alone

event.note: share B arrives with its end time in the past: ENDED (expired), A untouched

receiver_sequences.name: duplicate_start
receiver_sequences.why: the same row delivered twice is one row: the second is ignored and the end time is that of the first sighting

event.note: first sighting: endAt = min(R + 600, st + 1200) = T0 + 605
the same client message id again (a retry, a replay): ignored, endAt unchanged
one second before the first sighting's end
ENDED (expired): the duplicate did not extend it

receiver_sequences.name: stop_control
receiver_sequences.why: a stop applies only when it names a row of the same conversation and comes from the author of that row; it is idempotent

event.note: a stop from anyone but the author of the row (the receiver's own account) is dropped silently
a stop from anyone but the peer that names no known row is dropped silently and nothing is remembered
the share is untouched: ctr 2 accepted
the stop from the author: ENDED (stopped), key and positions deleted
frames after a stop match nothing

receiver_sequences.name: stop_after_expiry_keeps_the_first_reason
receiver_sequences.why: the first reason sticks: a stop that arrives after the end time does not turn 'expired' into 'stopped'

event.note: the share expired at T0 + 60; the late stop changes nothing

receiver_sequences.name: delete_for_everyone
receiver_sequences.why: deleting the start row for everyone ends the share; only the author of the row can

event.note: a delete not from the author is dropped
ctr 1: the share is still running
ENDED (deleted): the row is handled by the delete path, no live-share card (no_card), the same result as a delete that arrives before its start

receiver_sequences.name: frames_that_are_dropped
receiver_sequences.why: authentication failures, bad lengths and invalid plaintexts are dropped without touching the share; a bad plaintext does not advance the counter

event.note: sealed for the opposite direction: authentication fails
ctr 1 with a reserved flag bit: authenticates, plaintext invalid
the valid ctr 1 is accepted: the invalid ones did not advance the counter
a final frame that carries a position: plaintext invalid, the share goes on
a final frame with another flag: plaintext invalid

receiver_sequences.name: approximate_and_extreme_positions
receiver_sequences.why: the APPROX flag, negative values and the extremes pass through; the fix time is the receipt time minus age

event.note: a start whose fix is approximate (ap 1), 7 s old: fix time T0 + 3
the smallest values, precise, a fix 65535 s old

receiver_sequences.name: frame_at_the_end_time
receiver_sequences.why: a frame received one second before endAt is applied; at endAt the share is over and the frame is dropped

receiver_sequences.name: stale_then_expired
receiver_sequences.why: no frame ever arrives: STALE after 121 s, ENDED at endAt

receiver_sequences.name: staleness_follows_the_announced_interval
receiver_sequences.why: STALE after max(3 x iv, 120) seconds: 180 s in low-power mode, 1800 s for a tolerated iv of 600

event.note: start, the default interval is 30 s
iv 60: the next frame is announced in 60 s
iv 10: the threshold is the floor, 120 s

receiver_sequences.name: stop_before_start
receiver_sequences.why: a stop that overtakes its start (they travel on different lanes) is remembered, and the start is then created ended: no key, no position

event.note: the stop arrives first and names no known row: it is remembered for DU_MAX + SKEW seconds (a tombstone)
the start arrives: ENDED (stopped) on creation, k is never stored
no key was kept: nothing matches

receiver_sequences.name: delete_before_start
receiver_sequences.why: a delete for everyone that overtakes its start is remembered like a stop: the start is created ended with the reason deleted

event.note: the start arrives: it is handed to the delete-for-everyone path as if the delete had come after it, so no live-share card is shown (no_card); the record is ENDED (deleted) and k is never stored

receiver_sequences.name: stop_before_start_survives_a_restart
receiver_sequences.why: the memory of a stop is durable: a start that arrives after the receiving process restarted is still created ended

event.note: the process restarts: the tombstone is read back

receiver_sequences.name: stop_before_start_only_from_the_peer
receiver_sequences.why: only the peer's stop can apply to the peer's start: a control from anyone else that names no known row is dropped and nothing is remembered

event.note: from the receiver's own account: dropped, no tombstone
a delete from anyone but the peer: dropped, no tombstone
the start arrives and the share runs

receiver_sequences.name: tombstone_is_kept_for_du_max_plus_skew
receiver_sequences.why: a tombstone lives DU_MAX + SKEW = 87000 seconds; after that no start can still be live, so forgetting it changes nothing

event.note: the stop arrives first: remembered until T0 + 87005
one second before the end of its time: still remembered
the start of a 24-hour share delivered after that: over on arrival anyway (expired), not live

receiver_sequences.name: tombstones_are_bounded
receiver_sequences.why: a receiver remembers at most 16 targets per conversation, the oldest forgotten first

event.note: stop 1 of a start not seen yet
stop 2 of a start not seen yet
stop 3 of a start not seen yet
stop 4 of a start not seen yet
stop 5 of a start not seen yet
stop 6 of a start not seen yet
stop 7 of a start not seen yet
stop 8 of a start not seen yet
stop 9 of a start not seen yet
stop 10 of a start not seen yet
stop 11 of a start not seen yet
stop 12 of a start not seen yet
stop 13 of a start not seen yet
stop 14 of a start not seen yet
stop 15 of a start not seen yet
stop 16 of a start not seen yet
stop 17 of a start not seen yet
the oldest target was forgotten when the 17th arrived: its start is live
the newest target is remembered: its start is created ended (stopped) and does not touch share A

receiver_sequences.name: reload_then_replay_old_frames
receiver_sequences.why: lastCtr and lastFrameAt are durable: after a restart an old frame is still old, and staleness still counts from the last frame

event.note: the process restarts: the share is read back with lastCtr 3 and lastFrameAt T0 + 90
a replay of ctr 2 (it authenticates): dropped, the position stays ctr 3's
121 s after the last frame (T0 + 90): STALE, the clock of staleness went through the restart

receiver_sequences.name: reload_without_the_counter_ends_the_share
receiver_sequences.why: a receiver that cannot restore lastCtr ends the share: it never resumes with a counter of 0, which would accept a replay of every frame

event.note: the process restarts and the record of the share cannot be read: ENDED (state_lost), key and positions deleted
a replay of ctr 2: nothing matches
even a new counter matches nothing: the share is over

receiver_sequences.name: restarted_sender_reuses_a_counter
receiver_sequences.why: a frame whose counter was already applied is dropped even when it authenticates and is final; the share ends by the stop, by a final frame with a new counter, or at endAt

event.note: a final frame under counter 1 again: authenticates, but the counter was already applied: dropped, the share goes on
a final frame under counter 3 again: dropped
the stop ends the share: ENDED (stopped)

receiver_sequences.name: receiver_blocks_the_sender
receiver_sequences.why: blocking the peer ends and wipes every share received from it; frames that follow match nothing

event.note: the user blocks the peer: ENDED (blocked), key and positions deleted

receiver_sequences.name: clock_a_day_ahead_then_a_correct_start_supersedes
receiver_sequences.why: shares are ordered by min(st, R): a start from a clock one day ahead is ordered by its arrival, so the correct start that follows supersedes it

event.note: share A: the sender's clock is a day ahead; endAt = R + du, ordering time min(st, R) = T0 + 2
the clock is corrected and share B starts: its ordering time T0 + 120 is not below A's: A becomes ENDED (superseded), B runs

receiver_sequences.name: clock_ahead_within_skew_then_a_new_start_supersedes
receiver_sequences.why: a sender clock 500 seconds ahead (within SKEW) does not make its share outrank the next one either

event.note: share A: st = T0 + 500 seen at T0: ordering time T0
share B, started 60 s later by the same clock after it was set right: ordering time T0 + 60: A becomes ENDED (superseded)

receiver_sequences.name: receiver_clock_behind_older_start_wins_accepted_limit
receiver_sequences.why: ACCEPTED LIMIT of min(st, R): the ordering assumes a roughly correct receiver clock. With the receiver clock behind the sender's, a prompt start is ordered by R (the receiver's clock) and a delayed older start by st (the sender's); when the gap between the two shares is smaller than the offset the older start supersedes the newer. It needs reordered starts AND a skewed receiver clock; it is pinned, not fixed

event.note: share B starts at the sender's time T0 + 60 and arrives promptly at the receiver's time T0 - 38 (the receiver's clock is 100 s behind: R is below st): ordering time min(st, R) = T0 - 38

share A, started at the sender's time T0 (60 s before B), is delayed and arrives at the receiver's time T0 + 100: ordering time min(T0, T0 + 100) = T0, not below B's T0 - 38, so A supersedes B although B is the newer share (accepted)

receiver_sequences.name: tombstone_repeat_does_not_extend
receiver_sequences.why: a target that is already remembered is not added again and its time is not extended; the tombstone is forgotten at exactly its arrival + TOMBSTONE_KEEP

event.note: the stop arrives first: remembered until T0 + 87005
the same target again: no new target, the time is not extended (until stays T0 + 87005)
a delete for the same target: the first reason (stopped) and the first time stand
one second before the end of its time: still remembered
its start finds no tombstone: over on arrival (expired), not stopped

receiver_sequences.name: same_sid_new_id_is_a_duplicate
receiver_sequences.why: a start that repeats the sid of a share the store holds is a duplicate even under a new client message id: it never resets the record, so a relay cannot replay the earlier frames into a fresh share with lastCtr 0

event.note: the same body (same sid and k) under a new client message id, a retry written as a new message: start_duplicate, nothing is created, replaced or reset, lastCtr stays 2
a replay of ctr 1 by the relay: frame_old

receiver_sequences.name: same_sid_after_the_share_ended
receiver_sequences.why: an ended record keeps its sid (not secret, only k and the positions are wiped): the start redelivered under a new client message id is a duplicate and does not bring the share back

event.note: the final frame: ENDED (stopped), key and positions deleted, the sid and the client message id kept
the same sid under a new client message id after the end: start_duplicate, the share stays ENDED
a replay of ctr 1: nothing matches, there is no key

receiver_sequences.name: a_start_born_ended_still_owns_its_sid
receiver_sequences.why: a share created ENDED (here expired on arrival) is a record too: its sid is remembered, and a start with that sid under a new id is a duplicate

event.note: ENDED (expired) on arrival, k never stored, the sid recorded
the same sid with a fresh st under a new client message id: start_duplicate, no live share is created

receiver_sequences.name: redelivered_start_after_a_restart
receiver_sequences.why: the duplicate test reads the live-share store, not only the message table: after a crash that kept the record but not the message row, the redelivered start (same client message id) is a duplicate and lastCtr is not reset

event.note: the process restarts: the live-share record is read back with lastCtr 2
the start is delivered again: start_duplicate, the record is neither replaced nor reset

receiver_sequences.name: reload_without_the_key_ends_the_share
receiver_sequences.why: a receiver that cannot load k of a share it holds ends it (state_lost): it does not leave it ACTIVE or STALE until endAt with a key it cannot use

event.note: the process restarts, the counter is read back but the key cannot be loaded (a Keychain item missing after a restore, an invalidated Keystore key): ENDED (state_lost), positions deleted
still ENDED (state_lost), not ACTIVE or STALE until endAt

sender_sequences.name: share_with_the_final_frame_on_the_tick
sender_sequences.why: no frame before the echo, one frame per tick and never closer than 10 seconds, the stop goes out at once and the final frame on the next regular tick

event.note: the user confirms: a fresh key, counter 1
no frame before the msg_sent echo
5 seconds after the last frame: one frame per tick, never closer than 10 seconds
the user stops: loc_stop goes out at once, the final frame waits for the next tick (the cadence is not disturbed), k is still held
the final frame carries counter 3; k and the counter are deleted
the share is over: nothing is built

sender_sequences.name: final_frame_at_once
sender_sequences.why: a sender that cannot wait sends the final frame at once, and it is exempt from the 10-second minimum

event.note: the process is ending: loc_stop and the final frame (counter 2) go out now, 2 seconds after the last frame

sender_sequences.name: restart_never_builds_a_frame
sender_sequences.why: a process that starts again and finds a share that was live builds no frame for it, position or final: the key and the counter died with the process that held them; it sends loc_stop only

event.note: the process was killed and starts again: loc_stop only, no frame, nothing is resumed
no frame for the old share
a stop of the old share has nothing left to do

sender_sequences.name: restart_between_the_stop_and_the_final_frame
sender_sequences.why: the stop already went out: a restart before the tick builds no final frame and sends no second stop

event.note: the user stops: loc_stop sent, the final frame waits for the tick
the process restarts before the tick: no final frame, no second stop

sender_sequences.name: stop_before_the_start_left_the_device
sender_sequences.why: a start that never left the device is withdrawn from the outbox: the peer never hears of the share, and no stop is sent

event.note: the user confirms, the start waits in the outbox
the user stops: the start is withdrawn, no loc_stop, no frame, k deleted

sender_sequences.name: stop_before_the_echo
sender_sequences.why: a stop never overtakes its start: it waits for the echo, and no frame is built for a start that was not acknowledged

event.note: the start leaves the device; no echo yet
the user stops before the echo: loc_stop is deferred, k deleted, no final frame
the echo arrives: loc_stop goes out now

sender_sequences.name: restart_before_the_echo
sender_sequences.why: a restart before the echo: the stop waits for the echo like any stop, and no frame is built

event.note: the start leaves the device; no echo yet
the process restarts: loc_stop is deferred, no frame
the echo arrives: loc_stop goes out now

sender_sequences.name: restart_before_the_start_left
sender_sequences.why: a restart while the start still waits in the outbox withdraws it

event.note: the process restarts: the start is withdrawn, nothing is sent

sender_sequences.name: a_second_share_starts_with_counter_1_and_a_new_key
sender_sequences.why: counters belong to a share: a new share has a new key and starts at 1, and the old share builds nothing more

event.note: share 2: a fresh key, counter 1 under it

sender_sequences.name: socket_down_builds_no_frame
sender_sequences.why: a frame is built only while the socket is up: a tick while it is down is skipped and the counter does not move; the first tick after reconnection builds the next counter

event.note: the tick while the socket is down: no frame is built, next_ctr stays 2
again: still no frame, still counter 2 next
the next tick builds counter 2 with the newest fix: nothing was queued and no counter was used while offline

sender_sequences.name: write_failure_consumes_the_counter
sender_sequences.why: a sealed frame has consumed its counter whether or not the write succeeded: the next frame carries counter n+1, never n again with a newer fix

event.note: counter 2 is sealed and its write fails: the counter is spent, next_ctr is 3 (a client that advances only after a successful write, or gives the counter back, says 2 here and seals counter 2 again on the next tick); the same bytes may be written again, a new frame under counter 2 may not

sender_sequences.name: write_fails_then_the_socket_drops
sender_sequences.why: the usual way a write fails is a socket that dies under it: the frame sealed before it keeps its counter, the ticks while down build nothing, and the first tick after reconnection carries the next counter

event.note: counter 2 is sealed and its write fails: the socket dies under it, next_ctr is 3
no frame: the socket is down, next_ctr stays 3

sender_sequences.name: final_frame_write_fails_is_never_retried
sender_sequences.why: the final frame is best effort: sealed under its counter, its write fails, nothing is sealed again and the stop that already went out is the end

event.note: the sender cannot wait: loc_stop goes out and the final frame (counter 2) is sealed, its write fails; k is deleted
nothing is built: no second final frame, no frame under counter 2 or 3

sender_sequences.name: stop_while_the_socket_is_down
sender_sequences.why: a share that ends while the socket is down builds no final frame: the loc_stop (durable) is the end and the key is deleted at once

event.note: the user stops: loc_stop goes out through the durable path, no final frame is built, k deleted
nothing is built: the share is over

sender_sequences.name: socket_drops_before_the_final_frame
sender_sequences.why: the final frame waits for a tick and is built only while the socket is up: a socket that drops first takes the final frame with it, and the key goes

event.note: the user stops: loc_stop sent, the final frame waits for the next tick, k still held
the socket drops before the tick: the final frame is dropped, k deleted
nothing is built: no final frame under a counter after the end

end_time_cases.name: prompt_delivery
end_time_cases.why: delivered at the sender's start time: endAt = R + du

end_time_cases.name: late_by_10_minutes
end_time_cases.why: delivered exactly SKEW late: st + du + 600 = R + du

end_time_cases.name: late_by_11_minutes
end_time_cases.why: delivered 11 minutes late: the sender's clock bound ends it 60 s earlier than R + du

end_time_cases.name: late_by_two_hours
end_time_cases.why: delivered two hours late: already over on arrival

end_time_cases.name: sender_clock_9_min_behind
end_time_cases.why: the sender's clock is 540 s behind: within SKEW, endAt = R + du

end_time_cases.name: sender_clock_11_min_behind
end_time_cases.why: the sender's clock is 660 s behind: the share ends 60 s early on the receiver (a safe failure)

end_time_cases.name: sender_clock_9_min_ahead
end_time_cases.why: the sender's clock is 540 s ahead: R + du is the bound

end_time_cases.name: sender_clock_11_min_ahead
end_time_cases.why: the sender's clock is 660 s ahead: R + du still bounds the share, it is not stretched

end_time_cases.name: sender_clock_a_day_ahead
end_time_cases.why: a clock a day ahead cannot stretch a share

end_time_cases.name: sender_clock_a_day_behind
end_time_cases.why: a clock a day behind: over on arrival

end_time_cases.name: st_zero
end_time_cases.why: a sender clock that was never set: over on arrival
